question.text: Let $R$ be the set of real numbers and the functions $f: R \rightarrow R$ and $g: R \rightarrow R$ be defined by $f(x)=x^{2}+2 x-3$ and $g(x)=x+1 .$ Then, the value of $x$ for which $f(g(x))=g(f(x))$ is

solution.text:
According to question,
$$
f(g(x))=g(f(x))
$$
$\Rightarrow \quad f(x+1)=g\left(x^{2}+2 x-3\right)$
$\Rightarrow \quad(x+1)^{2}+2(x+1)-3=x^{2}+2 x-3+1$
$\Rightarrow \quad x^{2}+1+2 x+2 x+2-3=x^{2}+2 x-2$
$\Rightarrow \quad x^{2}+4 x=x^{2}+2 x-2$
$\Rightarrow \quad x^{2}+4 x-x^{2}-2 x+2=0$
$\Rightarrow \quad 2 x+2=0$
$\Rightarrow \quad 2 x=-2$
$$
\Rightarrow \quad x=-1
$$
